newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais hold on to coffee, defaults likely -trade.
newsitem.headline: Thais hold on to coffee, defaults likely -trade.

text.p: Thai coffee market was void of offers but full of bids as sellers held on to limited stocks, hoping to make the most of current surging world prices, traders said on Thursday.
Industry sources said they expected to see some contract defaults if the prices remain bullish.
Robusta faq (fair average quality), Thailand's only export grade, was bid around $2,050-2,100 per tonne FOB Bangkok as the London July robusta contract surged to $2,260 per tonne on Wednesday night.
"It is a sellers' market right now. Despite high bidding prices, no one wants to sell outright. They expect to sell at the best prices," said one Bangkok-based trader.
"There is not much coffee left, perhaps 2,000 tonnes, hence no offers. They would rather wait," he said.

"There will be some defaults as the prices now are so tempting. But the extent would be limited. There are not many players in this market and once you default, it will be hard to do business in the future," said the trader.
